narration: We start on the left with the inputs to the pipeline.
First input: a reconstructed 3D point cloud of the indoor scene.
Second input: the set of posed RGB images captured in that scene.
Third input: the matching depth images together with their camera poses.
Step 1 of the method performs 3D-aware 2D mask tracking.
From the point cloud, a superpoint is selected as the 3D seed region for an object.
The superpoint is projected into every view, and a histogram of the projected points counts how well each view sees it.
The peak of that histogram picks the pivot view: the frame where the object is most visible.
The pivot view and the projected points are fed to SAM 2 for segmentation, producing a 2D mask in the pivot view.
That mask, plus 3D cues from the scene, initialises SAM 2 tracking.
Tracking runs bidirectionally from the pivot view: a backward pass and a forward pass across the image sequence.
The result is a 2D mask track: the same object segmented consistently across all frames.
Step 2 refines these tracks into 3D proposals via mask optimisation.
The 2D mask track is lifted back into 3D to form a 3D mask candidate.
The candidate is refined by the optimisation of Algorithm 1, yielding the final 3D proposal.
Collecting the refined proposals gives a class-agnostic 3D instance segmentation of the whole scene.
Finally, CLIP and an LLM label those instances, producing open-vocabulary and open-ended 3D instance segmentation.
